question: How can a Stellar smart-wallet user receive and use USDC without first holding XLM for transaction fees and account reserves?

golden.answer: A C-address can hold USDC through its Stellar Asset Contract balance without a trustline reserve, whereas a G-account needs activation and trustline reserves unless sponsored. A fee bump or relayer pays transaction fees, and beginSponsoringFutureReserves/endSponsoringFutureReserves assigns eligible reserve liability to a sponsor. Costs shift to the sponsor rather than vanish, and Stellar has no universal native paymaster.
keyFacts: A C-address holds USDC via its SAC balance with no trustline reserve.
A fee bump or relayer pays fees; begin/endSponsoringFutureReserves shifts reserves.
Gasless onboarding shifts cost to a sponsor; Stellar has no universal native paymaster.
avoid: Do NOT claim gasless onboarding eliminates all costs rather than shifting them.
Do NOT claim a classic account holds issued USDC without a trustline.
Do NOT call USDC on a C-address a separate wrapped asset.
golden.notes: Token-paid relay and hosted facilitators are provider designs; grade later sourced changes leniently.
